translations.text: Again, just as I did not tell you who
they are, or what all the other things written in all the letters are.
And perhaps this is the likeness of those chains of darkness in which God bound the angels who abandoned their authority and cast them down into Hades, having revealed himself
in bonds and bandages, with them bound in him or fastened to him with fetters and a covering, like those imposed on Sodom and Gomorrah.
And perhaps this, too, is the form of what he said: “I will stretch out my sandal over Idumea.” He manifested himself in straps and bandages, trampling on them.
That is why I told you, brothers, in the house of God, before the altar, on the day when we did bitter things,
Stop your weeping! Stop! Whether you have wept or have not wept, the sword has already become drunk in heaven. It is strong and stretched out in the hands
of the one who was entrusted with it, ready to slaughter. It will turn and come upon this Edom, about which I spoke to you in another letter.
But those living in it did not believe until the sword came and destroyed them, because they did not take precautions when they heard the sound of the trumpet, as the prophet [?].
say it, nor did they believe the one who first told them
“Do not let those who live in Judea rejoice.”
For the one whose identity they do not know is looking into the distance, ready to stamp his sandal down upon those in Idumaea and those who practice deceit in its midst with filthy pleasures.
Does every person [?]?
[?] like the one about whom it was said, “For honey drips from the lips of a prostitute; afterward you will find her bitter as wormwood.”
Was it not because of those who wasted away from this disease, or whom this disease consumed, that anguish weighed down upon the prophets from the beginning like a stone,
as they said, “They tormented my life in a pit; they placed a stone upon me. Waters poured over my head. I said, ‘He has abandoned me.’”
So he did not abandon him, as they say: “I called upon your name, Lord, from a pit below. You heard my voice.
Do not close your ears to my plea. You came near to help me on the day when I called upon you. You told me, ‘Do not be afraid.’ You pleaded the cases of my soul, Lord; you redeemed my life.
You saw my troubles, Lord, for you saw them, and I did not hide them from you. You judged my case.”

Nor, for its part, does what they say about those wasting away in this wasting disease mean that it was their own will that took hold of them, to intensify it or not intensify it within them until it gained strength in their bodies.
They said, “You will repay them, Lord, according to the works of their hands.
You will repay them with suffering according to the strength of their hearts.
You will pursue them in your anger and destroy them from beneath heaven, Lord.”
Or are the prophets speaking about an actual stone when they say that it was placed on them?

Or are they not saying this about the sickness of anguish in which they find themselves, or which is within them and has weighed down on them like a stone, because of those whom they see stricken with this pestilential disease?
And they also said, “They placed a stone on me,” because of the blows dealt to those people, which torment their souls to the point of death.
For they were killed.
How can anyone say that the prophets do not share in the anguish that rests upon them because of those who are wasting away, or who waste away at any time, in this disease,
since they themselves foresee both what is happening and what will happen?

Not only do they see from afar what will happen to people on earth before it happens, but they also foresaw or understood what will happen to sinners on the day of wrath, and what will happen to the righteous,
as the one who speaks through them, who is God, says: “My servants will eat. My servants will drink. My servants will rejoice. My servants will shout with joy.”
But you will hunger. But you will thirst. But you will be put to shame. But you will cry out because of the anguish of your hearts, and you will howl because your spirits are broken.”
Whom is he addressing as “you,” except those who will die wasting away in that pestilential disease?
It was concerning these two diseases—the disease of punishment and that of all who wallow in that evil disease, for which the disease of punishment, or of Hades, will one day take hold
of everyone who dies persisting in it, or with it persisting in them—that the prophets said in the suffering of their anguish: “My heart is broken within me; they trembled,
all my bones. I became like a broken man, and like a man overcome by wine, before the Lord and before the greatness of the beauty of his glory.”
“For the earth is full of adultery. The earth mourned in the face of these things.”
As he also says, “I mourned over the brokenness of the daughter of my people.”
In the shadows, pains overwhelmed me, like a woman about to give birth.
Or again, “My heart, my heart causes me anguish.”

Not only did the prophets and all the righteous suffer anguish, sorrow, and groaning, or suffer the pain of anguish because of those suffering from the whole disease of lawlessness, but the Savior too,

the Lord of all, when he became human for the salvation of humanity, himself also suffered, just as all the righteous suffered anguish because of our sins, through the disease into which we have all fallen.
But he took upon himself all our diseases, or the evils that had come upon us, as Scripture testifies: “He is the one who bore our sins
and all our afflictions,” so that sin might not rule from that moment onward over those who would be freed from the disease of every kind of lawlessness. And as for those who have not been freed
from the disease of sin, he will return to them once again their sins, which he took upon himself or bore, because they did not remember how a crown of thorns was placed
on his head. Nor did they remember that the prophets, the apostles, and all the righteous endured agonies, or fell into agonies, because of our sins.

If someone wants to rescue people from great affliction and save them from deep anguish, and those people in turn hide themselves from him in his affliction and anguish, they themselves know that they are rejoicing.
O you alone, God, whose works are all truth and righteous judgments, who know the distress of this sickness that has put my poverty to the test!
For I recognized my sins through your teaching, or through your instructing me.

My heart and belly are full of fire, or have been set on fire by the heat that presses into them from the fever of that evil disease, which burns in both my ribs, this one and that one, and my other [?], and also my feet.

For this reason I cannot refrain from saying this other bitter or harsh statement, namely: Not only will I celebrate this Passover with you, or among you, as a stranger, but I will also spend the remaining days
of my life looking after my own life as a stranger, as I have already said in other letters written to you all, because of those who practice, or have now practiced,
these pestilential and abominable deeds among you, whether male or female—and not because of you yourselves, the holy brothers and sisters among you, whether male or female, old or young.
For just as judgment, bloodguilt, and other, still greater miseries fall upon the one speaking to you if he makes himself a stranger to you yourselves,
beloved, so too judgment and bloodguilt fall upon him if he maintains friendship with those who do, or who will do, corrupt deeds among you.
Instead, their judgment and their bloodguilt fall upon themselves because of the resolve of the one who does not agree with them.

For this reason, whether he bears this disease or does not bear it, its stench must not rise or spread. Rather, he must remain covered, or be covered over, until the extremity of his foul stench reaches
his garment. And even if he assembles with the whole congregation in every activity, in every way, under every commandment of God, he is an enemy of those who have not obeyed, or who will not obey,
the words and commandments that God commanded in his congregations, so as not to let a person who has that disease upon him scratch himself, in order that they may find relief or be healed of it.

But they have also scratched it among themselves with many kinds of scratching, laughing, having scratched themselves along with it through its activity, which is [?], with scratching until its sores multiply.
They did not fear God. They felt no shame before people. They had no pity on themselves.
Nor did they think that their sins would return upon their heads, and their acts of ungodliness upon the tops of their heads.
Did they not also know that the distress and sorrow of the one who turns his heart toward estrangement from them, or toward hostility, would return and fall upon them?

For they did not believe what he said in other letters, where the written word of God says this: “Who will make a holy place foreign to God through his corrupt deeds?” As he says, “You have made this place foreign to me.”
And that God should not make those people strangers to himself, whether male or female, who commit or will commit abominations at any time within his congregations.

This favor is not due to you, you deceitful people—that God has not withdrawn from his holy places because of your abominable deeds. Rather, it is due to his mercies and to the faithful brothers who live among you.
If people make room for estrangement from God through their impiety, people also make room for God to draw near to them through their righteous deeds, and for God to bring them near to himself.
For stop letting this man, whose identity you do not know, take secrets he possesses, or which you do not understand, and mix them with things not revealed to me—these things, like blood
that has been poured onto blood and taken up after they have mingled together, and sprinkled down from above onto the heads of these people and into the midst of the assembly
of those others who commit, or will commit, abominable deeds in his synagogues at all times, with the words that the Lord spoke to his disciples having been fulfilled
upon the unclean men and unclean women who are, or will be, among you: “Shake off the dust of your feet against them as a testimony against them.”
And that they are children of hostility, not children of peace.
For peace and those appointed masters over peace know who is worthy for their peace to rest [?] upon them [?]
and who is unworthy, so that it should not rest upon them, but peace should return to itself, or to the places it knows, which it makes its resting places
upon them, fulfilling, or taking the place of, the Lord’s disciples at all times until the end of the age, just as he commanded them:
“As for the children of peace, let your peace rest upon them. As for the children of hostility, let your peace turn away from them and return to you.”
Or is Peace not the companion of the righteous?
And is the spirit of the righteous not the companion of Peace?
And those with whom Peace will be will become sons of peace and daughters of blessing.
And those against whom Peace will be hostile will become sons of hostility and sons of the curse.
Oh, woe to you, those who have destroyed their virginity and their worth among you, and have defiled their endurance or the works of their endurance!
Your killers are not human killers. Rather, they are killers arising from your very selves.
That male pig and that wild boar [?], of whom they spoke [?] concerning [?] in Scripture, are the ones who ruined your soul and devoured it with their teeth and tusks.
The congregations have become filled with groaning, weeping, and cries: “Oh, oh! How long will they go on committing these abominations in God’s holy places?”
And: “Do not do these pestilential deeds.”
At all, in any way. And yet you did not listen, until your heart died [?] Hades [?] or this illness [?] evil [?] truly [?] its stings [?] through the scratching that is sweet for the moment.
For you have not blunted its sting or its stings, you false virgins, whether male or female, among you—those who will commit abominations within the congregations at any time.
What will you say before those who tormented death and conquered death by striking it with their virginity or their worthiness, and destroying its sting—or whose sting
was destroyed before them through their true righteousness—when death has tormented you by conquering you through its defilements, its impurities, its thefts, and its other pestilential deeds?
Or will someone who remembers the evil deeds you have done not spit out bile and become like those outside?
How will you mock death, saying, “Death, where is your victory? Hades, where is your sting?” when it has destroyed your hope, or you have destroyed it through death by your evil deeds?
You yourselves bear witness against yourselves through them, as to what sort of things, or what things, you have done after all those commands from God.

You boast [?]. He [?] that [?] you [?] him [?] we [?] to him: “Death, where is your victory?” Or rather, “Where is your victory?” Or, “Hades, where is your sting?” As though [?] truly! Or rather, where is your power?
which he destroyed,
or which she destroyed through the poison of his sting, which she spread.
Wrath, anger upon anger, curse upon curse, judgment and bloodshed upon judgment and bloodshed, upon the heads of those who do or will do these wicked deeds among you at any time!
Likewise, mercy upon mercy, blessing upon blessing, grace upon grace, power upon strength, upon the heads of those who do or will do righteous deeds among you at any time!
Or in what way is that expression, “Repay” or “Take vengeance,” excessive compared with the many such things I have said in my anguish,
which I said while you listened, brothers, in the place where we sat on the mountain outside the assembly, near the rock or the wall?
For I sent for you again today so that you might understand that sorrow is bitter, just as you saw its bitterness increasing around
the place about which I told you, “God did not speak with me,” so that no one should think anything beyond what he hears from me.

But this is the place where they put a stumbling block beneath me to prevent me from coming in to you on the day that I told you which it was, and that even now there are stumbling stones on the road.

And concerning this I said, “Just as I have not gathered with you in uprightness or unity of heart to pray, or indeed to examine a word of God, for more than seven months now, I will not gather now either.”
And why is that?
Is it not because of the [?] people whom God made strangers to us within two months because of those pestilential deeds that we have not ceased doing even now, whether men or women?
How could they not be bitter?
The sorrow whose bitter deeds bear witness to it, or are mixed with it like something sweet mixed with much bitterness, which takes away the sweetness in it.
Just as we tore the tunics and ripped those of the sisters who sinned among us, like soldiers, because they sinned against their king, Jesus.
We pursued them and drove them out from among us, although they were our brothers and sisters, our children, our fellow servants, and our fellow soldiers of the one Lord, God, the King, the Almighty.
Oh, the great sorrow!

For if it is a sorrow that God has thrown out of his congregations those who were caught committing abominations among us, although they will not lack bread and water in whatever place each one wished to go,
Then how great is the sorrow in the place where we will go, when we see those who will die in the deceitful deeds they do secretly in those synagogues being thrown
out of the resting places in the kingdom of heaven into the fire that is never extinguished, the place where there is no water and no bread, where there is no comfort at all.
Listen to this statement, and let us pay attention to it.
Those who die, or those who will die among us—will we say of them all
that they are righteous, or that they are virgins, or that they have entered into life, or that they have received the crown?
The prophet says, “He put on a robe of vengeance”—that is, God—“and his anger, like repayment, will repay his enemies with wrath.”
“And those who hate you, he will repay them.”
The one who dragged Esau down, namely God, as the prophet says, “I dragged Esau down; I uncovered their hidden things,” when they could not
hide—he is also the one who drags down, or will drag down, those who commit, or will commit, defilements, impurities, and every deceitful deed among you now, you synagogues.
He exposed their hidden things, and they could not hide—from God, not from people.
Understand what you are saying, you who kill yourselves with the knives of sin, which are all your deceitful deeds:
“If we are visible to people in our abominable deeds but hidden from God in our evil deeds, then let each one, every person, carry out his lawless acts.
For what will they do to me or to you if they know our evil deeds or learn about them?”

If our sins are hidden from people but visible to God, then in many ways and by many means he will expose the impurities, the defilements, and every deceitful deed that we commit or will commit in these congregations at any time.
Is it not a disgrace and a great [?] for the congregation that our fathers gathered together through hardships?
They established it through suffering, through the one who gave them strength, Jesus, if I speak according to what is written:
“That [?].”
